expressibility_gap.invariant: derivable: R_k = R_i ∩ R_j for another pair of rules
expressibility_gap.why: the extracted table's rules are disjoint singleton cells, so every pairwise intersection is empty and no non-duplicating derivable insertion exists — the expectation is recorded as unreached rather than forced into the table

expressibility_gap.invariant: a sampled conventional review can evidence every injected fault class
expressibility_gap.why: spot checks resolve values, not rule-space coverage: dead duplicates and widened rules leave the sampled cells' caps unchanged

discrepancies: Source scope: the annex PDF is not in the bogart corpus read surface (corpus_attachments empty; the exact values appear on 0 serving pages) — the grounded artifact is a recon text extraction, recorded so no corpus-level claim is implied.

Extraction hazard: the PDF text layer prints `Alcance: Zona Desfavorable` AFTER its three rows; the extraction maps the label backwards, and the naive row-order artifact is one of the injected faults (the dead duplicate).
The annex declares no precedence; the extracted table is disjoint, so the base document declares no policy. PriorityOrder/DeclaredDisjoint appear only in injected fault documents.
procedure: 1. The extracted table, its provenance (annex text sha256), the fault set, and the sampled conventional review were committed in fixtures/probes/rule_lens/ before any run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/rule_lens_extracted_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: the review a team performs on an extracted table — a sampled (scope, date) value check resolved under the document's declared policy, four of six cells above the floor and the single floor cell.
3. The probe arm ran `catherine rules` over the declared finite domain on the same fault documents; findings are the CLI's verbatim output.
4. A fault is caught only when the arm's output evidences it; unique detections are the lens findings on faults the sampled review missed (the rule-lens P8 comparison procedure, unchanged).
5. The verdict follows harness::derive_probe_verdict: zero unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
